Diego — quick legal read below. Quoting your suggested workaround for context:

> - Redwood provides an interim COI naming "Acme Health, Inc." as an Additional Insured within 3 business days of countersignature.
> - Redwood's broker will deliver the formal Additional Insured endorsement within 21 calendar days after countersignature (endorsement to match COI naming).

We can accept the interim COI + 21-day endorsement in principle, with the following clarifications and constraints:
1) Entity naming: please use "Acme Health, Inc., its subsidiaries and affiliates" only if Acme confirms that language. Otherwise we should mirror the exact corporate entity Acme provides. Broad "and affiliates" language increases potential exposure; request that Acme confirm corporate hierarchy.
2) Waiver of subrogation: do not agree to broader waivers on primary coverage unless underwriting approves — redlines asking for broad waiver flagged.
3) Endorsement deliverable: require an ISO CG 20 10 or equivalent additional insured endorsement for CG where available; if carrier declines, require written broker confirmation explaining limitation.
4) Cyber limits: Redwood's standard acceptance is $1M; if Acme requires higher, we need underwriting sign-off.

Please have Aditya record the interim COI commitment as a commercial exception on the deal and add a 21-day endorsement follow-up task in HubSpot. I attached a short COI template and suggested endorsement language for our broker.

-Kim
